text:
maria: trying to run the python sample app locally (poetry v1.4.0) and `poetry install` bombs on the redwood-sdk wheel + typing stuff. Any quick fixes?

jason: what error do you see? pip/poetry output helps. mac/ linux/ci?

maria: on mac (M1), during `poetry install` i get a fallback to sdist and then build fails: 
```
ERROR: Failed building wheel for tokenizers
ERROR: Could not build wheels for tokenizers which use PEP 517 and cannot be installed directly
```
also mypy errors later because `typing-extensions` is pinned to 4.5.0 in the lockfile and py3.12 wants >=4.7.

jason: OK two things: 1) the wheel platform mismatch on mac M1 is usually because the published wheel is manylinux-only. pip falls back to building tokenizers from source which needs rust toolchain. Quick workaround: install the binary tokenizers wheel first with `pip install tokenizers --only-binary :all:` (or brew install `rust` before build).
2) for typing issues you can override in your venv: `pip install \"typing-extensions>=4.7\"` — that resolves mypy/runtime typing mismatches until we fix the lockfile.

linh: adding: if you're using an editable/dev install with poetry (`poetry install --no-root` / `--develop`), compiled extensions don't get prebuilt. For local dev I usually do: `poetry export -f requirements.txt -o reqs.txt --without-hashes && pip install -r reqs.txt` so pip handles wheels. poetry 1.6.x also has better editable handling; upgrading helped for me.

maria: thanks — tried `pip install tokenizers --only-binary :all:` and it skipped the build but then redwood-sdk still fails because it wants `typed-ast` pinned and mypy complains. sample app's lockfile pins a very old `mypy`/`typing-extensions`.

ashley: hitting the same in CI (GH actions on ubuntu-latest). job log snippet: 
```
Collecting redwood-sdk==0.13.2
  Using cached redwood_sdk-0.13.2.tar.gz (22 kB)
  Preparing metadata (pyproject.toml) ... error
  ERROR: Command errored out with exit status 1: python setup.py egg_info
```
Then later `ERROR: Failed building wheel for redwood-sdk` — CI fails because we don't pre-wheel everything in the workflow.

jason: we should update the sample-app repo to include a `wheelhouse/` of prebuilt wheels for CI or change the workflow to build wheels first: `pip wheel -r reqs.txt -w wheelhouse && pip install --no-index --find-links wheelhouse -r reqs.txt`. That avoids rust/pegen build steps during CI runs.

maria: +1 to wheelhouse, that would make onboarding much smoother. Also, can we relax the typing-extensions pin in the example lockfile?

linh: I'll open a small PR to bump typing-extensions and move tokenizers out of strict pins. Also will add a note to README recommending `poetry self update` to 1.6+ or using the `poetry export` workaround.

devx-bot: opened issue #1423: \"sample-app: packaging failures on mac M1 and CI due to wheel pins and old typing deps\". Workarounds: `poetry export` -> `pip wheel` -> `pip install --no-index --find-links`, or upgrade to Poetry 1.6.x. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/issues/1423

ashley: i can add the GH actions `pip wheel` step in the CI patch — will do after #1423 is created.

maria: thanks all — this unblocked me locally (used pip install overrides) but the sample app should definitely land the wheelhouse + lock tweaks. :thumbsup:

jason: follow-up: we might also publish macos universal2 wheels for the SDK in the next release; i'll sync with release lead.

maria: great, marking this resolved on my side.
